newsitem.title: USA: Bankers Trust deal depended on new Fed rule.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust deal depended on new Fed rule.

text.p: The decision of the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise a limitation on how much underwriting can be done in a securities affiliate of a commercial bank holding company was a key factor in the proposed acquisition of broker Alex. Brown Inc by Bankers Trust New York Corp, Bankers Trust chairman and chief executive Frank Newman said in a telephone conference call Monday.

The change, effective earlier this year, allows revenue from underwriting in a "Section 20" affiliate to be as much as 25 percent of the revenue of the securities affiliate. Previously, the limitation was 10 percent.

Newman said on a pro forma basis, underwriting for the two firms combined would have been about 20 percent of securities revenue, so the combination would have been "clearly well in excess" of the old 10 percent limitation.
Newman said the the Bankers Trust-Alex. Brown deal was the "first major investment banking combination" of its kind since the Fed "modernized" its rules.
The Federal Reserve has also moved recently to relax certain "firewalls" between a bank and a securities affiliate. Newman said that change cut down on "needless overhead."

Section 20 refers to the Glass-Steagall law enacted after the onset of the Depression. The rationale at the time was that if banks were to offer deposit insurance, they should stay out of "risky" areas like securities. But Newman said "I don't think Glass-Steagall was a good idea even when it was enacted." He added, "I think the lending business is much riskier than underwriting."
Newman said corporate clients need a mixture of financial services, and combining Bankers Trust's specialties with those of Alex. Brown would make things easier for the client.
Newman said the deal combined Bankers Trust's expertise in syndicated bank debt and debt securities with Alex. Brown's equities research, distribution and underwriting.
He said while each company could have built up the specialty where it was not dominant, "building is very long and hard."
Newman spoke to the teleconference from Canada, where his 27-year-old son was hospitalized after a mountain climbing accident. He said his son had a "bad fall" but "he's going to be fine."
